messages:
olga: Hey team — prepping a POC with ProspectCo (migration from competitor X). Need quick alignment on blocker list and who owns each. TL;DR: they want a drop-in adapter, parity for prompts + responses, SSO/KMS, and clear pricing delta.

sam: thanks. can we confirm the API surface they use? full prompt + metadata?

olga: yep. they send { prompt, user_id, session_id, max_tokens, temperature, safety_level } and expect the same response envelope with choices[].text and usage.

mira: probably fine, but note tokenization and stop-seq behavior differs across models — we should capture that in the test harness.

devon: on adapter: we can do a thin proxy that maps their envelope to our /v1/generate and back. main concerns: rate limit semantics and streaming vs non-streaming compatibility.

olga: can you sketch limits we should advertise? they asked for 99th perc latency targets too.

devon: propose: burst 200 rps, sustained 50 rps for Dedicated POC. 99th < 150ms for short responses (<64 tokens) on equivalent hardware. caveat: depends on batching.

jamie: pricing question: customer wants per-call parity vs per-token. do we have a migration offer?

sam: sales motion: recommend 3-month trial with usage credit and include a one-time adapter dev credit. highlight predictable committed rate pricing for Dedicated after POC.

kai: security checklist — they need SSO (SAML), KMS integration for keys, audit logs, and contract-level SOC2/SCC. Are we comfortable with connector requirements?

mira: KMS is available for Private and Dedicated. For Hosted we can offer bring-your-key via customer-cloud KMS (requires engineering uplift). note: audit log retention is configurable but longer retention is an add-on.

olga: customer also filled a security questionnaire asking about response caching and PII controls. need short answer drafts.

kai: draft for caching: "We implement prefix and KV caching configurable per-route; sensitive routes can disable caching. PII should be filtered client-side, and we recommend tokenization redaction rules." I'll drop a one-paragraph we can use.

devon: regarding prompt parity: differences will arise from tokenizer and special tokens — recommend creating a 200-case prompt suite that covers stop tokens, leading spaces, and long-context splits. run diff harness comparing choices[].text and our choices[].text with normalization rules.

mira: add a fuzz test for the EOS/stopping behavior and one for deterministic seeds (temperature=0).

olga: perfect. who can own the test harness and initial mapping table?

devon: eng owns harness. I'll allocate a sprint task and snapshot expected diffs. estimated 3 days to get baseline.

sam: I'll prep the SOW language for the adapter + 3-month trial. Need the eng ETA and security paragraph by EOD Wednesday.

kai: I'll send the security questionnaire answers by tomorrow noon.

jamie: I'll draft a pricing note: convert their per-call budget into tokens using conservative estimates and include buffer for stop-token variance.

olga: thanks — next steps: devon implements initial proxy + harness, kai finalizes sec answers, sam + jamie produce commercial terms. I'll sync with ProspectCo on timeline and get their staging API creds.

deploy-bot: deploy 2245007-adapter-sprint created by devon — due 3 days from now. :rocket:

mira: one more — capture a sample discrepant output to illustrate user-visible UX delta. helps legal & PM sign-off.

olga: good call. I'll ask ProspectCo for 20 representative requests. tagging @devon for visibility. :thumbsup:
